question: Can the same graph add context-dependent foraging while keeping its nonlinear three-object learning ability, and does alternating developmental practice improve this outcome?
start: All three schedules start from the same ordinary 64k hard-triangle graduates, each cohort's six full inherited graphs with a fresh common Adam. All lifetime writing permissions remain open.
experience: Each schedule contains the exact same ordered set of 4000 old triangle updates and 4000 target context/odor/mark updates. Compare old then new, new then old, and balanced shuffled pairs (one of each per two updates). Only their interleaving across training lives changes. Old tickets pay the actual choice after three experiences. Target tickets reuse the existing short-to-long physical resource curriculum with the target-local update count. Moments are carried across both domains. No optimizer acts during deployment.
evaluation: Report ordinary independent-object tests and the native held-out conflict quest on each identical frozen graph. Primary transfer challenge is one uninterrupted life that actually studies three rotated objects, two context-specific values and a feeder mark, then queries six actions from one common final snapshot before receiving any new taste. Cross all 64 private laws, both orders and interspersed supports; include no-write and uniform-action controls. Separate the six-way conjunction, its two component tasks and ordinary single-task behavior. Developmental recurrence and within-lifetime acquisition are distinct.
comparison: Use both cohorts of six trained bodies and new held-out world seeds. The checkpoint after a single blocked strand has half the total updates and is a milestone, not an equal-budget final comparator. No new architecture or task selector.
